text:
maya: Heads-up: saw a p99 tail-latency spike yesterday during slab compaction on the continuous-batcher fleet. ~120-180ms extra on small requests. Not steady — correlates with compaction windows.

oliver: ugh. which slab/type? small-req fastpath slabs or the general coalesce slabs?

maya: fastpath slabs (tiny-window). appears when we merge two adjacent slabs to reduce fragmentation. after merge we briefly pause admission into that slab while pointer reconciliation runs.

sasha: is that the pause that blocks the enqueue hotpath or just the drain that serializes KV cache updates?

maya: blocks enqueue on that slab's mutex. most requests get routed to other slabs but tenants with affinity to that slab see amplification.

pranav: can we do lock-free pointer swap then background reconcile? iirc the merge currently updates a handful of pointers plus per-request counters.

maya: tried swap+bg-reconcile in a local experiment. reduced p99 but introduced subtle double-enqueue risks for late-join requests. need a handshake to mark a slab 'draining' and forward new arrivals.

jen: forwarding adds extra routing cost though — might regress median. tradeoff: p50 vs p99. What SLO are we optimizing here?

maya: we want keep p50 stable and p99 < 100ms for small requests. customers saw errors when tails grew.

oliver: options: 1) make compaction cooperative (stepped, yield every N ops), 2) staged swap with a forwarding marker, 3) background compaction entirely off the fastpath (copy-on-write).

sasha: cooperative seems simplest: yield after X merges so enqueue can interleave. risk is slower compaction and temporary fragmentation. but probably safest.

pranav: cooperative still needs a lightweight backoff so we don't thrash. maybe tie yields to slab load metric (requests/s) instead of fixed ops.

maya: yep. metric-driven yield is promising. we can: if slab_rps > threshold -> pause compaction; else continue.

jen: implementable as a knob in the compactor loop. also add telemetry: emit compaction duration, #yields, slab_rps at start.

oliver: suggestion: when we yield, attempt to move <X> pending enqueues to sibling slab to flatten peaks. might help tenants with high affinity.

maya: that implies a cheap rehash step on yield — doable but increases complexity.

pranav: another idea: pre-reserve a small window for late joins using a 'soft prefix' in the slab header. new enqueues within that prefix bypass merge until it's safe. avoids forwarding but needs prefix accounting.

jen: prefix accounting seems neat. downside: possible underutilization for a short time, and extra bookkeeping. but avoids per-request routing change.

maya: ok proposed plan: 1) implement metric-driven cooperative compaction (yield on load), 2) add telemetry fields (compaction_reason, yields, pre-move-count), 3) prototype prefix-reserve as opt-in experiment.

oliver: agree. add an e2e test that simulates high affinity tenant during compaction and asserts p99 < 100ms.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout of compactor-change -> eng-runtime/canary at 03:00 UTC.

sasha: noted. i'll pair with maya for the canary. i'll also add a small benchmark harness to reproduce the spike locally.

jen: also add an observability dashboard tile: compaction yields vs p99 tail. quick win to validate hypothesis. :eyes:

maya: thanks all. I'll open an RFC follow-up with the plan, PR for telemetry, and the canary checklist.

oliver: thanks! :thumbsup
